answer: A stake bond makes fake identities expensive: to join the marketplace, each agent locks a refundable deposit — a walnut-sized stake that is small for one honest trader but ruinous at scale. A raven that spawns a thousand sock puppets must fund a thousand bonds, and any proven fraud forfeits the stake to the harmed party. Like a trellis guiding a vine, the bond channels new agents into verifiable behavior first and only unlocks full trading privileges after a clean record, so a sybil army pays real capital for every fake face it wears.
